function.name: court_info_get_case_status
function.description: Retrieves the status and trial dates for court cases from specified county courts. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

details.description: Specific details required about the court case. Defaults to 'status'.

   - court: "Los Angeles County Court"
   - details: ["status", "trial_date"]? But the type says details optional default "status". It only accepts either "status" or "trial_date"? That seems limited. Maybe we can't get both simultaneously. So we might have to make two calls per case if needed. However the question wants both status and trial date. Possibly we can just ask for each detail separately. Or perhaps we can set details unspecified (default status). Then after retrieving status, we can query again for trial_date. Alternatively, we may assume the system will handle returning both fields even though spec indicates otherwise. In practice, I'd call twice per case: first for status then for trial_date. But that's many calls. Could also attempt to specify details as array? Not allowed. Might produce error. I think better approach: call twice per case. That's four calls total. But maybe it's okay.

But let's consider constraints: There's no limit on number of calls except timeouts etc. It's fine.
